# VS Code Copilot Release Brief: 2026 Q3

> **Stage:** Published routing artifact under the approved WP3 durable-owner decision. This records accepted ownership; it does not by itself authorize archival of `vscode-latest`.

## Routing Status and Acceptance Evidence

| Change family | Canonical owner | Status | Acceptance evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Surface and execution selection | `surfaces` | Accepted | Surface router owns context, control, review, and Ask Questions steering boundaries. |
| Model and provider configuration | `copilot-primitives` | Accepted | README owns Manage Language Models, BYOK, custom endpoint, utility-model, and sign-in boundaries. |
| Organization model and tool policy | `enterprise-patterns` | Accepted | README owns model policy, OpenTelemetry export, and curated/off MCP governance. |
| Multi-session coordination | `copilot-app` | Accepted, existing coverage | Existing owner retains session visibility, isolation, steering, and integration review. |
| Closed-loop browser validation | `copilot-web` | Accepted, existing coverage | Existing owner retains observable browser and UI evidence for delegated work. |
| CI response and trust signals | `agentic-sdlc` | Accepted, existing coverage | Existing owner retains actionable failure evidence, stop conditions, and rerun criteria. |
| Runtime portability | `copilot-sdk` | Accepted | README distinguishes application-owned runtime, editor-hosted UX, remote Agent Host evidence, and AHP coordination. |
| External-client integration | `copilot-acp` | Accepted, existing coverage | Existing owner retains client, permission, protocol, and session boundaries. |
| Context compaction | `copilot-cli` | Accepted | README owns the compact/preserve/inspect decision without universal savings claims. |
| Compaction diagnostics | `copilot-chat-internals` | Accepted | README owns context-loss symptoms, supplied-context inspection, and constraint re-anchoring. |
| Execution defense in depth | `copilot-hooks` | Accepted | README separates hooks, approvals, preview OS sandboxing, and sensitive terminal prompts. |

## Time-Bound Changes

The current `vscode-latest` source tracks model providers, preview states, session UX, browser tools, and runtime infrastructure across VS Code releases. For future refreshes, verify these items against current VS Code release notes and record only changes that alter a durable owner’s decision, artifact, evidence, or boundary.

## Resolved Items

- **Context compaction and cost-quality tradeoffs:** routed to `copilot-cli`; diagnostic recovery routed to `copilot-chat-internals`.
- **Terminal sandboxing platform boundaries:** routed to `copilot-hooks` as one layer in a defense-in-depth decision.
- **Ask Questions interaction ownership:** routed to `surfaces` as a human-steering contract, not a standalone feature inventory.
- **External indexing for non-GitHub workspaces:** `retired-with-rationale`; no current durable setup contract was verified, so this brief preserves no setup guidance.
- **OpenTelemetry, MCP allowlists, and sensitive-prompt handling:** organization policy routed to `enterprise-patterns`; sensitive prompt and execution boundaries routed to `copilot-hooks`.

All WP3 items now have an accepted owner or an explicit retirement disposition.

## Retirement Checklist

- [x] Every routed claim is grounded in current first-party documentation.
- [x] Each canonical owner has accepted README coverage or retained existing coverage.
- [x] Every previously unassigned item has one disposition.
- [x] Durable README guidance is recorded for the WP3 owner edits.
- [ ] The old slug resolves to the brief or a frozen retirement page.
- [ ] The `vscode-latest` deck and companions are retired or redirected together.
- [ ] Catalog and inventory entries point to the replacement route.
- [ ] Builds, companion checks, and links validate after the retirement changes.

`vscode-latest` cannot archive until the redirect, deck and companions, catalog and inventory updates, and final validation are complete.
